key_insight: In metal-halide perovskites, localized carrier spin relaxation is dominated by hyperfine coupling, with holes generally relaxing via metal nuclei and electrons via halogen nuclei, and the exact dynamics depend strongly on the hyperfine correlation time.
engineering_relevance: A more accurate spin-relaxation model can improve interpretation of time-resolved spin experiments and help identify perovskite compositions with longer carrier spin lifetimes for optoelectronic design.
method: Adapted a muon-spin-spectroscopy relaxation model to localized carrier spins.
Solved longitudinal spin relaxation exactly across arbitrary hyperfine correlation times.
Fitted time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two perovskite samples to extract localization volume and correlation time.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the exact dynamical solution was applied to time-resolved Faraday rotation data from two samples and outperformed a single-exponential approximation in extracting microscopic parameters.
watch_item: The model targets localized carriers in an intermediate correlation regime, so applying a mono-exponential or fully delocalized approximation may misestimate spin lifetimes and localization parameters.
paper_title: Hyperfine driven spin relaxation of charge carriers in metal-halide perovskites
